claim: Every finite triangle-free simple graph G on n vertices contains a set S of floor(n/2) vertices with 50*e(G[S]) <= n^2.
owner: Sodelin project; classical, modern and independent audit agents
purpose: Settle the complete Erdos #128 conjecture. Reward verification is tracked separately and no eligibility or payment is claimed.
approach: First audit historical and current methods, exact scope and formal statement. Replay the published Clebsch obstruction to the three-part edge-neighborhood method. Select a new proof attack only after the reviews identify a genuine remaining gap.
search_queries: Erdos sparse half conjecture triangle-free graphs classical methods
More about sparse halves in triangle-free graphs

reward.acceptance_criteria: Foundation requires original published Erdos reward documentation and first community-accepted solution published in a reputable peer-reviewed mathematics journal. AI-assisted eligibility not explicitly established by sponsor rules.
reward.payment_trigger: Discretionary award after Foundation assessment; a correct Lean proof alone is not a payment trigger.

correctness.formal_statement_note: Existing Lean statement is category research open and contains sorry. Its cardinality guard is 2*|S|+1 >= n, matching floor(n/2). No full proof exists in our work.

history.detail: Intent: extensive classical/modern review and exact reproduction of a published method barrier. Literature checks and reproductions are review work; no new full-proof attempt is cleared yet.
